about: What scripts/test-drift.mjs may stop reporting, and why. A case the other side has and this tree does not is either coverage to bring home or the same property under other words — and the difference is a judgement nobody can make twice from the output alone. Each entry is that judgement, written once. `file` is a regular expression on the path as the other side spells it; `cases` narrows an entry to particular titles, for a file where only some of them are answered.

answered.note: settings-user-preferences.test.js here holds the same property — every writable preference round-trips through the route — and holds it better: it asserts the key is listed in NON_DEFAULT and fails with the remedy, where this one invents `true`, watches the sanitiser refuse it, and reports the key as dropped. A second gate over one property, with the worse message.

four cases against eleven here, each of the four a rewording of one of ours: a secret kept across a restart, one the operator set, where a generated one is stored, and an unusable one replaced without logging it. Ours also cover a staging file's permissions and a CONFIG_DIR that is not a directory.

eighteen cases against thirty-five here. Every property of theirs is asserted here under other words — the counter replay, a synchronised key's counter of zero, a changed signature byte, a key made for another domain, base64url — and ours add the curves, the key types, a missing coordinate, extension data and trailing bytes.

`should return ok status` and `should return ready status` are the original wording of what this tree asserts as the payload of /healthz and /readyz, inside cases that also hold the probes to answering without a session, without a store and without a cookie.
the same three assertions, each of ours naming the trash zone as well as the personal folders and the hidden paths theirs name.
`puts items in the chosen folder, and says how far it got` is ours with `and remembers the folder` on the end.

eight cases against twelve here, reworded one for one — including taking the handlers off again, which ours calls `leaves nothing listening` and which asserts more: that nothing is logged afterwards either. Deleting the two `off` calls in processFailures.js turns ours red, which is how this was settled after nearly adding the case twice.

cases: ^is the new password that signs in afterwards$
answered.note: brought home, and kept under a title that says the other half: `is the new password that signs in afterwards, and not the old one`.

cases: ^swipes through mixed media and swipes down to close$
answered.note: brought home, in the case named `swipes through mixed media, and a swipe down closes rather than navigating` — which keeps what ours already said about a vertical gesture not turning the page.
